fact: Teaching at Oxford existed in 1096. Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital, was founded in 1325 - 229 years later.
hook: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
source: Smithsonian Magazine / University of Oxford - teaching existed at Oxford in 1096; Tenochtitlan founded c. 1325.

fact: One spin of Venus takes 243 Earth days, but one orbit around the Sun takes only 225 Earth days.
hook: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
source: Nature Astronomy via The Hindu - rotation 243.0226 Earth days, orbit 225 Earth days.

fact: Saturn's average density is 0.687 grams per cubic centimetre, while water is 1 - so Saturn is less dense than water.
source: NASA / Cassini mission summaries - Saturn density 0.687 g/cm3 vs water 1 g/cm3.

fact: About 3 trillion trees grow on Earth. The Milky Way has only about 100 to 400 billion stars.
hook: There are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way.
source: Nature (tree count) / ESA Gaia - ~3 trillion trees vs 100-400 billion stars.

fact: Wombats are the only known animal that makes cube-shaped droppings. The cubes do not roll away, so wombats stack them to mark territory.
source: Georgia Institute of Technology research - intestines shape droppings into cubes; cubes stop them rolling away.

fact: A lightning channel can reach about 30,000 degrees Celsius. The surface of the Sun is about 5,500 degrees - so lightning is about 5 times hotter.
hook: Lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
source: US Dept. of Energy / weather references - lightning ~30,000 C vs Sun surface ~5,500 C.

fact: A desert is defined by how little rain or snow it gets, not by heat. Antarctica is extremely dry, so it counts as a desert - bigger than the Sahara.
hook: Antarctica is the largest desert in the world.
source: Standard geography definition - desert = low precipitation; Antarctica is the driest, largest desert.

fact: Light travels about 150 million kilometres from the Sun to Earth in about 8 minutes and 20 seconds.
hook: The sunlight you see left the Sun 8 minutes ago.
source: Standard astronomy - Sun-Earth distance ~150 million km, light travel time ~8 min 20 sec.

fact: More than 99 percent of everything in the solar system - planets, moons, asteroids and comets included - is in the Sun itself.
hook: The Sun holds almost all the mass in our solar system.
source: NASA - the Sun makes up 99.8% of the solar system's mass.

fact: The Moon has no wind, rain or flowing water to wear them away, so the footprints from the Apollo landings remain in the dust today.
hook: The astronauts' footprints on the Moon are still there.
source: NASA - no atmosphere/weather on the Moon, so Apollo footprints remain.
